name: Classical Hollywood
description: Studio-era filmmaking built on continuity editing, stars and genre, within which a few directors developed strong personal styles.

name: German Expressionism
description: Distorted sets, heavy shadow and subjective camera used to externalise inner states.

name: Soviet Montage
description: Editing treated as the essence of cinema: meaning comes from the collision of shots.

name: Poetic Realism
description: Fatalistic French stories of ordinary lives, shot with studio lyricism.

name: Italian Neorealism
description: Location shooting, non-professional actors and stories of ordinary people in postwar Italy.

name: Postwar modernist art cinema
description: Auteur-driven films that loosen plot and foreground ambiguity, subjectivity and form.

name: French New Wave
description: Critics turned directors who shot cheaply on location and broke the rules of continuity and tone.

name: Left Bank group
description: The literary, politically engaged wing of the French New Wave, preoccupied with memory and documentary.

name: Japanese studio golden age
description: The studio-era masters whose films reached the West in the 1950s.

name: Japanese New Wave
description: A generation that attacked the humanism of the studio masters with sex, politics and formal rupture.

name: Czechoslovak New Wave
description: Satire, non-actors and formal play under, and against, state socialism.

name: New Hollywood
description: A film-literate generation that brought European art-cinema methods into American genre film.

name: New German Cinema
description: Young West German directors confronting the national past with low budgets and personal styles.

name: American independent cinema
description: Directors working outside or at the edge of the studio system. A production context more than a shared style.

name: Taiwan New Wave
description: Long takes, distant framing and everyday life used to examine Taiwan's history and modernisation.

name: Hong Kong Second Wave
description: Auteur filmmaking that grew out of Hong Kong's commercial industry, restless in style and preoccupied with time and identity.

name: Korean New Wave
description: High-craft genre films that fold in social critique and abrupt shifts of tone.

name: Iranian New Wave
description: Poetic realism that blurs fiction and documentary, often through children and non-actors.

name: Dogme 95
description: A manifesto of handheld cameras, natural light and location sound, against technical polish.

name: Surrealism
description: Dream imagery and irrational juxtaposition aimed against bourgeois logic.

name: Spaghetti Western
description: Italian-made westerns that turned the genre operatic, cynical and violent.

name: Parallel Cinema
description: A realist alternative to mainstream Indian cinema, rooted in Bengali literature and neorealism.

name: Slow cinema
description: Very long takes, minimal narrative and attention to duration and stillness.

name: Transcendental style
description: An austere style that withholds expression and drama to point beyond the everyday.

name: Social realism
description: Working-class lives filmed with documentary methods and little stylisation.

name: Postmodern cinema
description: Pastiche, quotation and genre mixing, with irony about the film's own artifice.

name: Silent comedy
description: Physical comedy built from long, wide takes that prove the gag was really performed.

name: Romanian New Wave
description: Long handheld takes, real-time pacing and dark humour about life during and after Ceausescu.

name: Chinese Fifth Generation
description: The first class to graduate after the Cultural Revolution, turning to landscape, colour and history in place of socialist realism.

name: Chinese Sixth Generation
description: Low-budget, often unofficial films about contemporary urban and provincial China, shot in a documentary manner.

name: Cinema Novo
description: Brazilian political cinema made cheaply and roughly by design, mixing neorealism, folklore and agitation.

name: Greek Weird Wave
description: Deadpan, absurd allegories of family and power, delivered in stilted speech.

name: Film noir
description: Shadowy American crime films about fate, corruption and desire, shaped by German émigrés and hard-boiled fiction.

name: Hollywood musical
description: Studio films organised around song and dance numbers, at their height in MGM's Freed unit.

name: Screwball and sophisticated comedy
description: Fast, verbal Hollywood comedies of class, courtship and remarriage.

name: Silent-era pioneers
description: The directors who established feature-length storytelling, the epic and the star system before sound.

name: Soviet cinema after the Thaw
description: Soviet filmmakers who used the loosening after Stalin to pursue personal, poetic and often censored work.

name: French classical cinema
description: French studio-era craftsmanship outside the New Wave: polished scripts, genre films and poetic fantasy.

name: French post-New Wave
description: The generation after the New Wave, harsher or more extravagant than its predecessors.

name: Documentary traditions
description: Non-fiction filmmaking, from staged ethnography to direct cinema, testimony and the essay.

name: Avant-garde and experimental film
description: Artists' films made outside the industry that explore perception, duration and the medium itself.

name: British studio era
description: The peak of British studio filmmaking, from Ealing comedy to the Archers and David Lean.

name: British New Wave
description: Working-class stories and location shooting, growing out of the Free Cinema documentaries.

name: British art cinema
description: British directors working in a personal, formally adventurous mode outside the realist mainstream.

name: Contemporary Hollywood
description: The era of the blockbuster and the franchise, in which a few directors keep a recognisable signature at very large scale.

name: Horror
description: The genre of fear, from Universal's monsters to independent American horror and the Italian giallo.

name: Animation
description: Feature animation, from Disney's studio system to Studio Ghibli.

name: Third Cinema and African cinema
description: Militant, anti-colonial filmmaking from Latin America and Africa, defined against both Hollywood and European art cinema.

name: Italian political cinema
description: Investigative films about power, crime and colonial war, growing out of neorealism.

name: Spanish cinema under Franco
description: Films that spoke about Spain through satire, allegory and childhood because they could not speak directly.

name: Polish Film School
description: The first postwar generation of Polish directors, reckoning with the war and its myths.

name: L.A. Rebellion
description: Black filmmakers trained at UCLA who rejected Hollywood models for independent, community-rooted work.

name: New Queer Cinema
description: Independent films that treated queer lives with formal daring and without apology.

name: Hollywood comedy since 1960
description: Studio comedy after the classical era: parody, improvisation and the teen film.

name: Australian New Wave
description: A state-supported revival that produced both atmospheric art films and genre hits.

name: Mumblecore
description: Micro-budget American films about young adults' relationships, improvised with friends as actors and shot on cheap digital or 16mm.

name: New French Extremity
description: The critic James Quandt's term for French films that confront audiences with explicit sex and violence.

name: Berlin School
description: German directors, several trained at the Berlin film academy, who make cool, observational films about everyday life and drift.

name: New Argentine Cinema
description: Low-budget Argentine films that broke with the national industry through location shooting, non-actors and elliptical storytelling.
